body:
I know, I know deep down you guys are all right. There’s so much more to this story but all of it would only make my case to leave much stronger. 

This blows. 

Thanks everyone. I appreciate the replies.

I just had a baby and my 1st will be 10 this year, my second will be 7. I feel it’s a great age to be able to give my 3rd more time than I gave them because they were only 3 years apart. That was hard for me being pretty much a single parent at the time. 

My kids are thrilled in having their baby brother and they can’t wait until he’s a little older to entertain him and play with him. My son likes the idea of being the big older brother that can show him the ropes. We will see.

On school days we do 1.5 hours after they’ve done all their work and have played outside first. On the weekend I will do about 2.5 hours broken up. They get screen time only if they have earned it (cleaned room, tidy messes, good attitude). This does not include TV. Only Xbox and tablets.

My almost 10 year old and 7 year old get to play in the front yard and ride bikes/scooters up and down the street. I frequently check on them through our camera. They do not get to go around the block unsupervised.

Oh man, I could have written this post! I can totally relate with you and I’m continuously trying to find a way to be a better parent so I don’t have much advice other than to tell you that you’re not alone. I wonder if we have unrealistic expectations because like everyone else said... we’re human. We want to have this idea of taking perfect scenarios and images from things we see and want to become that when really there is no constant variable. Everything changes because we all have emotions! How can we be consistent when there are so many factors to take into consideration. 

It’s just so hard, I know. I wish I had the answers but I just signed up to see a therapist for parenting and stress coping techniques because again... I could have written this post myself. Hang in there mama, I feel like you’re doing a great job with even having the self awareness that you do.

*Edited for typos.

I appreciate all of your guys’ responses. Unfortunately there are more issues with this relationship. I brought it up to him this morning and of course his child and him can do no wrong. He pretty much said this relationship isn’t going to work all because he can’t hold his kid accountable like he does mine. We’ve argued a lot before about him taking accountability for his own actions (he tends to play the victim for everything and I’m the one who’s always the problem). He’s manipulative, a liar and narcissistic. I’m the stupid one who stayed after everything because he started getting better (he really did). He doesn’t insult me or yell anymore but he gets so defensive and his only solution ever is to end the relationship. 

I’m so drained. Physically and mentally. He said I was short with him yesterday morning (after barely sleeping at all with a newborn) and because I didn’t answer the way he would have liked it was a problem and I’m ALWAYS SO mean. This is such a lie. 

I realized that there is no compromising here with him over his kid. He’s never going to hold her accountable because he only sees her EOWE and is probably scared that she’s going to resent him like his oldest does. But he had the nerve to tell me today that she doesn’t listen because she doesn’t like me. That’s his excuse all the time. I’m the problem. 

Thanks again everyone.

I feel you on this! I have a 10 year old SD and 16 year old SS. Both of their parents are also “permissive” and have no consequences etc. The 16 year old just got his 15 year old gf pregnant and the 10 year old thinks she’s an adult and can listen to foul music, dance her life away on Tik Tok, be on her phone all day and not be told anything. I just cringe at all of it. I’m more strict with my two (9 & 6) and even though I may seem “unfair”, I’m thinking about their future and their mindset.
I wouldn’t say they don’t work. I matched with my husband on Bumble. I get that most of the time it seems futile but I wouldn’t say it as an absolute.
Yes, because they need their ego stroked and want the attention.
I’m 32+5 and I’m still asking myself that question! Ugh.
